I also checked the relevant Mathlib facts `Set.monotone_projIcc`, `Set.projIcc_of_mem`, `Set.projIcc_right` and `intervalIntegral.continuousOn_primitive_interval'` in the pinned Mathlib, plus the Mathlib idiom for transporting the primitive from `uIcc` to `Icc`. Two small, concrete simplifications are reported; neither replacement was compiled, and for the first one the proposed proof relies on the fact that the subtype order on `Set.Icc` coerces definitionally to the ℝ order (a `simpa`/`Subtype.coe_le_coe` fallback exists if elaboration is fussy).

findings.excerpt:
have hc : (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one s : ℝ) ≤ (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t : ℝ) :=
    max_le_max le_rfl (min_le_min le_rfl hst)
findings.problem: The proof re-derives monotonicity of `Set.projIcc` by unfolding it into a `max`/`min` and applying `max_le_max`/`min_le_min`. That mathematical fact is already a named Mathlib lemma, and re-deriving it forces the reader to know the definition of `projIcc` (and its `max (min x b) a` shape) to follow why `hc` holds. The very next lemma in the file already uses the named companion fact `continuous_projIcc`, so the file mixes two styles for the same object.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the two-line `have hc` proof by the named lemma:

```
  have hc : (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one s : ℝ) ≤ (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t : ℝ) :=
    Set.monotone_projIcc zero_le_one hst
```

(`Set.monotone_projIcc` yields the subtype inequality, which is definitionally the coerced ℝ inequality; if elaboration needs help, `simpa using Set.monotone_projIcc zero_le_one hst`.) The rest of the proof is unchanged.
findings.benefit: The key idea becomes explicit — clamping to `[0,1]` is monotone, so the integral over `[0, clamp s]` is below the one over `[0, clamp t]` — instead of an arithmetic `max`/`min` manipulation over an unfolded definition. It also matches the `continuous_projIcc` usage two lemmas later, so a reader sees one consistent vocabulary for `projIcc`.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem monotone_projIcc : Monotone (projIcc a b h) := fun _ _ hxy =>
  max_le_max le_rfl <| min_le_min le_rfl hxy

protected theorem Monotone.IccExtend (hf : Monotone f) : Monotone (IccExtend h f) :=
  hf.comp <| monotone_projIcc h

findings.excerpt:
have hi := spectralPathDensity_intervalIntegrable ρ eig hρ hρsum p a ⟨zero_le_one, le_rfl⟩
  have hp := intervalIntegral.continuousOn_primitive_interval' hi (a := 0) left_mem_uIcc
  have hp' : ContinuousOn (fun z => ∫ r in 0..z, spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r)
      (Icc 0 1) := by simpa only [uIcc_of_le zero_le_one] using hp
findings.problem: The proof threads three intermediate facts where only the last is used: `hi` is used only by `hp`, `hp` is used only by `hp'`, and `hp'` is the statement actually fed to `comp_continuous`. The names `hi`/`hp`/`hp'` thus add bookkeeping without exposing any additional mathematical step: `hp'` is literally `hp` transported across `uIcc_of_le zero_le_one`.
findings.proposed_change:
Collapse the three `have`s into one, folding the interval-integrability witness into the call and applying `simpa` directly to the Mathlib lemma:

```
  have hp : ContinuousOn (fun z => ∫ r in 0..z, spectralPathDensity ρ eig hρ hρsum p a r)
      (Icc 0 1) := by
    simpa only [uIcc_of_le zero_le_one] using
      intervalIntegral.continuousOn_primitive_interval'
        (spectralPathDensity_intervalIntegrable ρ eig hρ hρsum p a ⟨zero_le_one, le_rfl⟩)
        (a := 0) left_mem_uIcc
  exact hp.comp_continuous (continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_projIcc)
    (fun t => (Set.projIcc 0 1 zero_le_one t).property)
```
findings.benefit: The same construction is visible with fewer moving parts: the primitive of the density is continuous on `[[0,1]]`, hence (since `0 ≤ 1`) on `Icc 0 1`, and composing with the continuous projection gives continuity. This is exactly the idiom used in Mathlib's mean value theorem file, so the one-step form is recognizable rather than clever.
